prize_parts.citation: For the development of sequencing-by-synthesis chemistry, based on reversible terminators and clonally amplified single-molecule clusters, that made massively parallel DNA sequencing possible.

statement.case_for: I now propose a single-part prize for B017, credited to Balasubramanian and Klenerman. The scientific case is the one I accepted after the openings and that round 1 has reinforced: the reversible-terminator, fluorescent-nucleotide and surface-cluster chemistry is a genuine chemical invention, it has been independently confirmed for about two decades, and no member has argued that it is immature or conceptually thin. Five of eight round-1 files name it in a preferred configuration, and the support comes from members with quite different scientific viewpoints. The Cambridge pair is present in every B017 configuration, so it is the least contested attribution on the list. A citation that names the chemistry, the terminators and the clustered templates, makes explicit that the recognised discovery is a chemical method for reading nucleotide sequence in parallel, and answers the objection that it is merely a medical or biological tool.
statement.case_against: I have dropped my B003 part. In round 1 four members (Aqvist, Chabes, Sparr, Zou) independently pointed to the same difficulty: a Rees-only nitrogenase citation leaves out Dean, Seefeldt, Einsle and Ribbe, and any wider set breaks the three-person limit once B017 is included. The mechanism of N2 binding and reduction is still debated, so the defensible claim is structure and cofactor composition only, which is narrower than what I would want a second prize part to recognise. The chair's question about a joint motivation for two unrelated parts also has no good answer, and I will not add a part merely to carry a field I know well. The remaining weaknesses of B017 are real. Mayer, Ju and Rothberg have credible claims, the 454 and semiconductor lineage is left outside the citation, and Sanger and Gilbert were honoured in 1980, so some will see a scale-up of an earlier capability. I think the chemistry answers the last point, but it must be stated in the citation, and the other exclusions are a cost we accept with any cut at three people.

responses.point: Aqvist wants Pascal Mayer as a third laureate for clonal amplification, and says the Cambridge pair alone is the cleaner fallback if no defensible third name emerges. He also questioned whether I consider the nitrogenase mechanism settled.
responses.response: On nitrogenase you are right and I have acted on it: I do not regard the mechanism as settled, structure and cofactor composition are secure but that is not a full story, and I withdraw B003 as a preferred part. On Mayer I remain with the pair. Clustering is certainly integral to the platform, but from the material in front of us I cannot separate a clustering concept and filing from the experimental demonstration of clonal sequencing on surfaces within the Solexa work, and a laureate should rest on the second. I would accept a third name only if the expert reports show that Mayer's experiments, not only his concept, established the cluster approach before Solexa. Without that, the cleaner fallback you describe is my position.

responses.point: Somfai prefers B048, Pd-catalysed C-N coupling by Buchwald and Hartwig, with a clean two-person attribution, and argues that C-N bond formation is a distinct catalyst-design problem from the 2010 C-C prize.
responses.response: The attribution is indeed the cleanest on the list and the ligand-design and mechanistic work, oxidative addition, amine binding and C-N reductive elimination, is the kind of physical-organic understanding I value. The point I cannot settle is whether it is a new concept or a second chapter of the framework recognised in 2010, and Kosugi's tin-amide precedent has to be handled in the wording. You also note that the reach of sequencing is wider than that of a reaction used mainly by chemists. I keep B048 behind B017, but I think it is the strongest fallback if the committee cannot agree on a B017 laureate set, which is why I would rank it ahead of my own B003.

responses.point: The chair, Linke, supports a three-name B017 with Mayer for the clustered colony-array concept, and notes that a citation saying sequencing by synthesis would need to handle the pyrosequencing and semiconductor routes without looking arbitrary.
responses.response: I agree that the wording is the practical difficulty. My citation therefore names the specific chemistry, reversible terminators and clonally amplified single-molecule clusters, rather than sequencing by synthesis in general, so that it describes the Solexa chemistry accurately and does not claim the whole field. That is more honest about Rothberg's and Ju's routes than a broad phrase that excludes them by implication. On Mayer, I take your argument for a separable cluster concept seriously, but unless the reports show experimental priority I would keep the third seat empty rather than fill it on conceptual credit alone.

responses.point: Chabes places B017 first, argues the readout chemistry rather than the instrument is what changed the field, and says he cannot verify priority between Solexa and the earlier Mayer and Mosaic work.
responses.response: I agree, and as someone who measures nucleotides daily your point on the chemistry is the strongest answer to the Sanger objection: in 1980 the recognition was for the methods of reading sequence, while this is a different chemical solution, cyclic reversible incorporation with parallel detection of millions of templates. I share your uncertainty on priority and propose that we treat it as the committee's single open factual question rather than argue it from memory. Your remark on nitrogenase as a strong alternative rather than a first prize this year is one I accept.

responses.point: Sparr prefers B029 on phase separation as a new physical concept, and herself identifies contested in vivo evidence and the exclusion of Pappu and Mittag as the main weaknesses.
responses.response: Your own case against is the reason I keep B029 below B017. The founding observation and the multivalent phase diagrams are real physical chemistry, but you say yourself that the maturity and the demonstrated consequences are less settled than for sequencing, and I would not want the committee to endorse a concept whose edges are still being tested. If the committee later wants a second part, I would want it limited to the founding observation and the quantitative framework, but I do not think a second part is warranted now.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports show that Mayer's cluster work was experimental and prior to the Solexa work, which would change my view on a third laureate.
Whether the citation can state clearly that the recognised achievement is chemistry, and not appear to dismiss the 454 and Ju routes.
Whether members who preferred B048, B029 or B041 will accept B017 as the prize, since the chair asked and only Zou and Sparr have named it as an alternative.
statement.conflict_note: I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou; this is not a conflict on any shortlisted candidate. I previously disclosed scientific proximity to B003 as a biochemist of biological energy conversion; since I no longer propose B003 as a preferred part, this proximity is now only relevant to an alternative. I have no personal or institutional tie to any named candidate and no reason to recuse.
